cities.name: Marrakech
cities.tagline: The imperial red city and Morocco's main tourist hub.
cities.best: Mar-May and Sep-Nov (summer is very hot).

sights.note: Main square: storytellers, musicians and food stalls, best at sunset and night.
Maze of markets next to the square (spices, leather, lamps, carpets).
Landmark minaret beside the square. Non-Muslims see it from outside.
19th-century palace with courtyards and painted ceilings. Entry 100 MAD foreign adult (checked Nov 2026).
16th-century royal tombs. Entry 100 MAD foreign adult (checked Nov 2026).
Ruined palace with big courtyards and storks on the walls.
Old Quranic school with a carved courtyard.
Blue garden in Gueliz. 170 MAD garden only, 330 MAD with both museums, official ticket site only (checked Nov 2026).
Next to Majorelle. Book ahead.

sights.n: Day trip: Ourika Valley or Imlil
sights.note: Cool mountain air and walks, 1.5 h from the city.

stay: Medina riads: atmospheric, close to everything, can be hard to find at night (ask the host to meet you at the gate).
Gueliz (new town): modern hotels, restaurants, easy taxis.
Palmeraie and outskirts: resort hotels with pools, you need a taxi.
food: Djemaa El-Fna food stalls (prices are displayed; check drink prices before ordering)
Harira soup, tangia (a Marrakech slow-cooked meat dish), grilled meat and aubergines
Fresh orange juice stalls on the square
Chez Chegrouni on the square (vegetarian couscous, per Wikivoyage)
scams: If someone says a medina street is closed, ignore them. It is a known trick to lead you into a quiet alley.
Guides should show an official badge. Refuse unbadged 'helpers' who walk with you.
Taxi: insist on the meter (compteur). Petit taxi minimum is about 7 MAD in the day. If he refuses, take the next one.
Sit-down drinks on the square rarely have prices on menus. Ask first.
Solo travellers: be careful with drinks from strangers and with room service.
cities.transport: Walk inside the medina. Beige petit taxis in town (meter, max 3 passengers). Grand taxi or bus for trips out. Train to Casablanca about 2h40.

cities.name: Fes
cities.tagline: The oldest medina in use, famous for its tanneries, madrasas and craft.

sights.note: Leather dye pits. Watch from a shop terrace. Shop staff will push you to buy: be firm and polite.
14th-century madrasa, one of the religious buildings non-Muslims can enter. Entry listed around 20-30 MAD (sources differ).
Smaller but richly decorated.
Oldest university, founded 859. Non-Muslims see the gates from outside.

sights.n: Talaa Kbira street and the medina (Fes el Bali)
sights.note: Main walking street from Bab Boujloud into the old city. Green, orange and other marked walking trails exist.
Museum in an old funduq building.
Hill with the best panorama of the medina at sunset.
Fortress overlooking the old city.
Old Jewish quarter.
Former royal palace turned museum.

stay: Fes el Bali riads and small hotels: best location, narrow alleys.
Ville Nouvelle: modern, near train station, quieter.
Near Bab Boujloud: easiest entrance to the medina.
food: Bab Boujloud market streets for cheap food
Pastilla (Dar Tazi / Le Palais de Fes per Wikivoyage)
Maison Fassi, Cafe Clock (listed in Wikivoyage)
Fassi specialities: pastilla, seffa, rfissa
scams: Fake guides: look like you know where you are going. Many 'friendly' people lead you to shops for commission.
'This road is closed' is a common lie to redirect you.
Belek! Belek! means move: a loaded donkey is coming.
Tannery: do not accept a 'free' tour that ends in a shop. Agree on any tip first.
Lone women often get harassment in alleys: stay on busier streets.
cities.transport: Walk in the medina (no cars). Red petit taxis in town. Train to Meknes, Rabat, Casablanca, Tangier.

cities.name: Casablanca
cities.tagline: Morocco's big modern city. Home of the Hassan II Mosque.

sights.note: Guided visits for non-Muslims. 140 MAD foreign adult (checked Nov 2026). Check times at the ticket office.
Seafront strip with cafes and beach clubs.
Small old town near the port.
Calm 1930s quarter with shops and pastry makers.
Hispano-Moorish building (listed in Wikivoyage).
The only Jewish museum in the Arab world (per Wikivoyage).
Many 1920s-30s buildings around Mohammed V and the Central Post Office.

stay: Centre / Maarif: central, business hotels.
Near Casa Voyageurs station: convenient for trains.
Corniche: sea views, a bit far from the centre.
food: La Sqala (restaurant inside an old fortress, per Wikivoyage)
Patisserie Bennis Habous (famed pastries)
Seafood near the port (Taverne du Dauphin per Wikivoyage)
Spanish tapas at La Cocina (per Wikivoyage)
scams: Pickpocketing and moped bag-snatching are the main risk: hide valuables, hold your phone away from the road.
Red petit taxis: ask for the meter.
cities.transport: Tram (30 km, 49 stops). Red petit taxis. Train from Casa Voyageurs to Rabat, Marrakech and Fes. Al Boraq high-speed train to Tangier.

cities.name: Rabat
cities.tagline: Calm capital with a UNESCO medina, kasbah and royal sites.

sights.note: Blue-and-white old fort with views over the river and sea.

sights.n: Hassan Tower and Mohammed V Mausoleum
sights.note: Unfinished 12th-century minaret and royal tomb.
Roman and Merenid ruins with storks. Entry about 70 MAD general (sources differ; one reports 30 self-guided).
Calmer than other medinas.
Mint tea over the sea (listed in Wikivoyage).
Older, narrower medina across the river.
Large colourful seaside cemetery.

stay: Ville Nouvelle near the station: easy and central.
Medina: budget hotels.
Agdal: modern, quiet.
food: Sandwich and fish stalls near the medina
Cafe Maure at the Kasbah
Le Petit Beur for bstilla (listed in Wikivoyage)
scams: Rabat is considered safe. Normal care with valuables.
Blue petit taxis: ask for the meter.
cities.transport: Tram between Rabat and Salé (about 6 MAD in 2019, check now). Blue petit taxis. Train station Rabat Ville in the centre.

cities.name: Tangier
cities.tagline: Port city where Africa meets Europe, with medina, cafes and Cap Spartel.

sights.note: Narrow alleys and the Kasbah Museum in the former sultan's palace.
The two old squares that join the medina to the new town.
Famous cliff cafe with sea views (listed in Wikivoyage).

sights.n: Caves of Hercules and Cap Spartel
sights.note: Coast west of the city where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean.
First US diplomatic property abroad (listed in Wikivoyage).
14th-century traveller born in Tangier.

stay: Medina and Kasbah: riads and small hotels.
Ville Nouvelle / near Place de France: central.
Near the corniche: sea view.
food: Seafood in the port (see Wikivoyage)
Local cafes: cafe au lait is cheaper in places where locals sit
Street snacks and fresh orange juice
scams: Hustlers are common at the port and in the medina. Say a firm 'la, shukran' and keep walking.
Arriving by ferry: people offering to fill your immigration form want money. Do it yourself.
Check the exchange rate yourself before changing euros.
cities.transport: Walk in the medina. Blue and white petit taxis. Al Boraq high-speed train to Casablanca (about 2h17 in Nov 2026 timetable).

cities.name: Chefchaouen
cities.tagline: The blue mountain town in the Rif. Slow, walkable and photogenic.
cities.best: Spring and autumn. Nights are cold in winter.

sights.note: Walk the blue alleys. Go early morning for empty streets.

sights.n: Outa el Hammam square and Kasbah
sights.note: Main square with the old kasbah and Grand Mosque.
Waterfall and spring at the edge of the medina where locals gather.
Hill walk for the sunset view of the town.
Day hike in Talassemtane National Park. Needs a grand taxi from town.

stay: Medina guesthouses and riads: best atmosphere.
Near Bab el-Ain: easy bus and taxi access.
Book ahead mid-July to September.
food: Local breakfast of eggs, cheese, olives and tea
Baghrir pancakes with honey
Fish tagine (Chez Foad, Granada in Wikivoyage)
Baissara (pea soup)
scams: At the bus station, touts may say your hotel is closed or full. Check yourself by phone.
Overbooked hotels sometimes move you to another for commission.
Offers of hashish are illegal for you. Walk away.
cities.transport: Everything in town is on foot. CTM and other buses from Fes, Tangier, Tetouan. Grand taxis to Akchour.

cities.name: Essaouira
cities.tagline: Windy fortified port town: relaxed, with fresh fish and art.
cities.best: Spring to autumn. Wind is strong in summer.

sights.note: Sea ramparts with old cannons. Entry about 60 MAD (checked Nov 2026).
Small walkable medina with art galleries and woodwork shops.
Fresh fish sold at the dock.
Kitesurf and windsurf. Water is cold, wind is strong.
Walk south along the beach.

stay: Medina riads: small and calm.
Near the beach: sea views, windy.
Touts at the bus station offer cheap rooms: check the place first.
food: Grilled fish at the port stalls (pick your fish, agree the price first)
Argan oil products from women's cooperatives
Seafood tagine
scams: Fake 'hash brownies' sold near the square. Illegal and often fake.
Bus-station touts offering cheap riads: do not follow without checking.
cities.transport: Walk in the medina. Taxis cost a flat small fare in town (8 MAD day per Wikivoyage Jan 2024). Supratours and CTM buses to Marrakech and Agadir.

cities.name: Agadir
cities.tagline: Big beach resort in the south with sun nearly all year.

sights.note: Long wide beach.
Ruined fortress on the hill with city and sea views.
Berber crafts (listed in Wikivoyage).
Large covered market.
Surf village and river pools 20-30 min away.

stay: Beachfront hotels and resorts.
Talborjt: cheaper hotels (per Wikivoyage).
Taghazout: surf hostels.
food: Fresh fish near the port
Cheap restaurants in Talborjt
Argan and amlou
scams: Taxi: use the meter in petit taxis.
Beach vendors and quad offers: agree prices first.
cities.transport: City buses (small fare). Petit taxis. Supratours and CTM buses to Marrakech, Essaouira and the south.

cities.name: Meknes
cities.tagline: Imperial city of Moulay Ismail: big gates, calmer than Fes.

sights.note: Largest and most striking of the city gates.
Square between the medina and the imperial city.
Free to enter, non-Muslim access limited, check hours.
Huge granaries and stables of Moulay Ismail.
Madrasa with a rooftop view. Fee about 60 MAD in Wikivoyage 2018, check.
Entry 100 MAD foreign adult (checked Nov 2026).
Holiest town in Morocco, hillside views.

stay: Ville Nouvelle hotels near the train station.
Medina riads for atmosphere.
food: Market near Bab El Mansour (olives, fresh produce)
Rue Antsirabe for cheap Moroccan staples (Wikivoyage lists Ville Nouvelle restaurants)
scams: Hotel touts at the station: ignore.
Petit taxis: ask for the meter.
cities.transport: Blue petit taxis. Buses and trains to Fes and Rabat. Grand taxi to Moulay Idriss.

cities.name: Ouarzazate
cities.tagline: Gateway to the Sahara and Morocco's film studio town.
cities.best: Spring, autumn and winter. Summer is very hot.

sights.note: Old kasbah. Entry about 20 MAD (checked Nov 2026).
Film studio tour. About 60 MAD (one source, Nov 2026).
UNESCO ksar used in many films. See that page.
Palm oasis near town, by grand taxi.
Scenic road south to Zagora via kasbahs.

stay: Hotels along Avenue Mohammed V and near the main square.
Kasbah-style guesthouses outside town.
food: Cheap restaurants on Mohammed V
Saffron-flavoured tea in the Ouarzazate area (Wikivoyage)
scams: Taxi drivers may take you to a hotel for a commission. Ask for the hotel you chose.
Aït Benhaddou: ignore anyone claiming a 'fee' to enter the bridge.
cities.transport: Petit taxis (low fares). CTM buses from Marrakech (about 4-5 h). Airport with flights.

cities.name: Ait Benhaddou
cities.tagline: UNESCO fortified earthen village, famous from many films.

sights.note: Cross the river bridge and climb through the village.
Great views, free (Wikivoyage).
Earthen villages along the road.

stay: Auberges and kasbah hotels near the ksar. Many people stay in Ouarzazate instead.
food: Tourist cafes with terraces facing the ksar
Tagine, couscous
scams: Entry to the ksar is free or very low (sources say free to about 10 MAD). Ignore touts claiming a fee at the bridge.
Do not pay for parking beyond a small tip.
cities.transport: On foot inside. Grand taxi from Ouarzazate (shared).

cities.name: Merzouga
cities.tagline: Sahara dunes of Erg Chebbi, camel treks and desert camps.

sights.n: Erg Chebbi dunes at sunrise or sunset
sights.note: Walk or camel trek into the dunes.
Camp stay with dinner and music. Budget camps from about 150-350 MAD per person (one source, Aug 2026).
Birds, flamingos in early spring (Wikivoyage).
Local black Gnaoua music.

stay: Dune-edge lodges and kasbah-style guesthouses.
Camp: check what is included (dinner, breakfast, transport).
food: Most meals at your lodge
Berber pizza (khlii-stuffed bread)
scams: Almost everyone will offer a camel, quad or 4x4 tour for a commission. Book through your lodge or a known operator.
Be careful with strangers who show strong romantic interest (Wikivoyage warns of problems for foreign women).
cities.transport: On foot in the village. Private 4x4 or transfer from Fes/Marrakech. Long drive: plan 2 days from either city.

cities.name: Tetouan
cities.tagline: Andalusian-style UNESCO medina in the Rif foothills.

sights.note: Unique Andalusian-influenced old town, less touristy than Fes.

sights.n: Bab El Okla and the Ethnographic Museum
sights.note: Museum in the old gate.
House museum (listed in Wikivoyage).
Small old tannery.
Views above the city.

stay: Medina riads (e.g. Riad Dalia in Wikivoyage).
Budget hotels near Place Moulay El Mehdi.
food: Restinga and Dallas pastry shop (listed in Wikivoyage)
Spanish-style cafes
scams: Bus-station touts: only buy from the ticket window.
cities.transport: Walk in the centre. CTM and other buses from Tangier, Chefchaouen.

cities.name: Asilah
cities.tagline: Whitewashed seaside medina with murals and Spanish touch.

sights.note: Small clean medina with wall paintings by artists.

sights.n: Beaches north and south of town
sights.note: Long sandy beaches.
Sea views at sunset.

stay: Guesthouses in and near the medina.
food: Seafood restaurants along Avenue Mohamed el Hassani (Wikivoyage)
Paella and Spanish dishes
scams: Touts at the arrival offering rooms: check before accepting.
cities.transport: Train station is 2 km from town (Wikivoyage). Walk inside the medina.

cities.name: El Jadida
cities.tagline: Portuguese fortified city on the coast, popular with Moroccans in summer.

sights.note: UNESCO fortified city of the 16th century.
Underground cistern, famous light and reflections.
Crowded in summer.

stay: Small guesthouses and riads in the old town.
food: Seafood and cafes along the seafront
scams: Few reports. Normal care.
cities.transport: Buses and train from Casablanca. Walk in the old town.

cities.name: Dakhla
cities.tagline: Lagoon town in the far south: kitesurf, wind and desert beaches.

sights.note: Kitesurf and windsurf spot.
Day trips by 4x4 or rental car.
Hotels and nautical activities.

stay: Hotels around the lagoon and Pointe du Dragon.
Camps for kite and surf.
food: Fresh seafood and oysters (the Dakhla region is known for oysters)
scams: Do not leave marked roads: area has mined zones (Wikivoyage).
cities.transport: Fly to Dakhla (Royal Air Maroc and others) or long bus. Petit taxis are metered.

cities.name: Taghazout
cities.tagline: Small surf village north of Agadir.
cities.best: Oct-Apr for big surf, summer for beginners.

sights.n: Surf: Anchor Point and Hash Point
sights.note: Reef and rock point breaks, strong currents. Beginners need a school.
Easy walks along the coast.
River pools between Agadir and Taghazout.

stay: Surf hostels and guesthouses in the village.
food: Cafe Mouja and village cafes (Wikivoyage)
Fresh fish grill
scams: Main risks are in the water: rocks, reef and currents.
cities.transport: On foot in the village. Buses and taxis from Agadir.

cities.name: Imlil and Toubkal
cities.tagline: High Atlas base for trekking Toubkal, 1.5 h from Marrakech.
cities.best: Spring and autumn. Winter needs crampons and an ice axe above snowline.

sights.note: Easy walks near Imlil.
North Africa's highest peak. Use a registered mountain guide, check season and snow.

sights.n: Day hike to Armed or Aremd
sights.note: Short valley walk.

stay: Kasbah du Toubkal (Wikivoyage)
Local gites and guesthouses
food: Tagines and mint tea at guesthouses
scams: Unlicensed trek sellers in Marrakech: book from Imlil guides' office or a trusted lodge.
cities.transport: Grand taxi from Marrakech (Bab Doukkala area). Mule or foot beyond Imlil.

cities.name: Ifrane
cities.tagline: Alpine-style town in the Middle Atlas with cedar forests and macaques.
cities.best: Winter for snow, summer for cool weather.

sights.note: Tourist photo spot.
Walk in the woods near Azrou/Ifrane.
Forest walks (listed in Wikivoyage).

stay: Hotels in the centre. Budget stays are easier in Azrou (15 min away).
food: Cafes and pizza (Wikivoyage mentions several)
scams: Grand taxi drivers: agree the fare first.
cities.transport: Walk. Grand taxi to Azrou. Buses from Fes and Meknes.

cities.name: Taroudant
cities.tagline: Walled market town, called 'little Marrakech'.

sights.note: Walk or bike around the ramparts.
Arab souk and Berber souk, argan and spices.
Former palace, now hotel (Wikivoyage).

stay: Hotels near Place Assarag.
food: Cheap restaurants around the main square
scams: Few reports. Bargain politely in souks.
cities.transport: Bicycles are common. Petit taxis. Bus or grand taxi from Agadir (about 1 h 30).

cities.name: Zagora
cities.tagline: Draa Valley palm oasis with camel treks and the Tombouctou 52 jours sign.

sights.note: Famous photo spot.
Green pottery, ancient library 18 km south.

sights.n: Camel trek or palm grove walk
sights.note: Short trek into the dunes at Tinfou or palm walks.

stay: Palm grove guesthouses and kasbah hotels.
food: Simple cafes along the main street
scams: Agree the camel trek price and what is included before leaving.
cities.transport: Petit taxis (low fares). Buses from Ouarzazate and Marrakech (about 8 h).

cities.name: Sidi Ifni
cities.tagline: Quiet Spanish Art Deco coastal town.

sights.note: Spanish-built centre.
Relaxed beach town.
Big market.

stay: Hotels along the promenade. Book ahead for Christmas/New Year.
food: Fish stalls in the permanent souk (Wikivoyage)
scams: Few reports. Normal care.
cities.transport: Walk. Petit taxis.

cities.name: Al Hoceima
cities.tagline: Rif mountains meeting the Mediterranean, beaches and a national park.

sights.note: High limestone cliffs and rocky coast.
Quiet beaches, busy in August.
Alhucemas islands and Peñón de Vélez are Spanish-administered (Wikivoyage).

stay: Hotels near the bay.
food: Fresh fish and seafood
scams: Few reports. Normal care.
cities.transport: Buses from Tetouan, Nador and Fes (long). Airport has some flights.

cities.name: Larache
cities.tagline: Quiet Atlantic town with Spanish colonial feel and Roman ruins nearby.

sights.n: Place de la Liberation and Spanish quarter
sights.note: Cafe square, evening life.
8 km from town on the Asilah road.

sights.n: Kasbah and Fortress of the Stork
sights.note: Portuguese-era fortification.

stay: Budget hotels south of Place de la Liberation.
food: Shawarma and sandwich places; bakeries and juice stores
scams: Few reports. Normal care.
cities.transport: Walk. Petit taxis.

cities.name: Oualidia
cities.tagline: Calm lagoon village known for oysters.

sights.note: Calm water, good for swimming and walking.
The region is known for oysters. Choose a busy stall.

stay: Lagoon-side guesthouses.
food: Fresh oysters and grilled fish
scams: Agree prices for boat rides and oysters before ordering.
cities.transport: Bus between El Jadida and Safi. Walk in the village.

cities.name: Ouzoud Waterfalls
cities.tagline: Tall waterfalls in the Middle Atlas, a classic day trip from Marrakech.

sights.note: Walk down along the falls.
Short boat ride at the bottom. Agree the price first.
Monkeys live near the path. Do not feed them.

stay: Most visitors come as a day trip. Simple guesthouses near the falls.
food: Grilled fish and tagine at the terraces above the falls
scams: Agree prices for guides, boats and photos before you accept.
Keep food away from the macaques.
cities.transport: Grand taxi, organised tour or car from Marrakech (about 3 h) or Beni Mellal.

cities.name: Ourika Valley
cities.tagline: Green valley south of Marrakech with villages and waterfalls.

sights.note: Hike up from the village. Wear shoes with grip.
Stop at markets and gardens.

stay: Guesthouses in Setti Fatma and Oukaimeden.
food: Tagine and grilled meat at riverside terraces
scams: Hire guides only at agreed prices and ask first.
cities.transport: Grand taxi or tour from Marrakech (about 1 h to 1.5 h).

cities.name: Azrou
cities.tagline: Middle Atlas town next to cedar forests and macaques.

sights.note: Walk in the forest outside town.
Local carpets and cedar wood work.

stay: Budget hotels. Cheaper base than Ifrane.
food: Cafes and grills in the centre
scams: Agree grand taxi fares first.
cities.transport: Grand taxis to Ifrane (about 15 min) and Fes. Buses on the Fes to Midelt road.

cities.name: Erfoud and Rissani
cities.tagline: Date palm oasis town and gateway to Merzouga.

sights.note: Local marble with fossils. Compare prices before buying.
Big souk, busy on market days.
Drive or walk through the oasis.

stay: Hotels in town. Many travellers continue to Merzouga.
food: Date products and tagines
scams: Be careful with unrequested guides and fossil shop commissions.
cities.transport: Buses from Fes and Errachidia. Grand taxi to Rissani and Merzouga.

cities.name: Midelt
cities.tagline: Quiet stop between Fes and the desert, in the Middle Atlas.

sights.note: Small village about halfway to Fes, hiking and biking.
Cooking experience with village women (Wikivoyage).

stay: Hotel Restaurant Taddart is listed as the nicest in Midelt (Wikivoyage, older).
food: Sandwiches near the bus station (Wikivoyage, price may be outdated)
scams: Few reports. Normal care.
cities.transport: Walk. Petit taxi about 10 MAD (Wikivoyage, older).

cities.name: Tiznit
cities.tagline: Walled town known for silver jewellery.

sights.note: Berber silver. Compare shops and bargain.
Easy to walk.

stay: Small hotels in the centre.
food: Simple cafes and grills
scams: Bargain for jewellery. Ask for the weight price.
cities.transport: Walk. Local taxis about 7 MAD day and 10 MAD night (Wikivoyage, older).

cities.name: Safi
cities.tagline: Atlantic port city famous for pottery.

sights.note: Closed Tuesdays per Wikivoyage.
Workshops on the hill.
Surf lessons available at the north end.

stay: Riads in the medina near the sea.
food: Fresh seafood, tagines, couscous
scams: Few reports. Normal care.
cities.transport: Walk in the medina. Bus and train links to Marrakech and El Jadida.

cities.name: Nador
cities.tagline: Mediterranean city on the Mar Chica lagoon.

sights.note: Sea promenade.
Views and monkeys.
Lagoon beach.

stay: City hotels and a few resorts.
food: Fresh fish; grilled sardines at local places
scams: Few reports. Normal care.
cities.transport: Buses and trains to Oujda and Fes (long).

cities.name: Laayoune
cities.tagline: Largest city of the far south, desert coast and lagoon.

sights.note: Birdlife (Wikivoyage).
Reachable by car.

stay: Many hotels, fairly expensive (Wikivoyage). Cheaper ones south of the airport.
food: Standard Moroccan food; camel meat at butchers (Wikivoyage)
scams: Check current travel advice for the Western Sahara region before going.
cities.transport: Walk in the centre. Petit taxis. Flights from Casablanca.

cities.name: Volubilis and Moulay Idriss
cities.tagline: Roman ruins and Morocco's holiest town, easy from Meknes.

sights.note: Roman city with mosaics. Entry 100 MAD foreign adult (checked Nov 2026).
Famous mosaic at the site.
Hill town with sunset views.

stay: Most people stay in Meknes.
food: Cafes in Moulay Idriss
scams: Agree guide fees at the Volubilis entrance first.
cities.transport: Grand taxi from Meknes. Bring hat and water.

cities.name: Saidia
cities.tagline: Beach resort on the Mediterranean near the Algerian border.

sights.note: Long sandy beach.

stay: Resorts and apartments, busy in summer.
food: Seafood and cafes by the marina
scams: Book ahead in July and August.
cities.transport: Buses and taxis from Berkane and Oujda.

cities.name: Oujda
cities.tagline: Capital of the Oriental region in eastern Morocco.
cities.best: Not sourced. Check the weather before you go.

sights.note: Historic medina gate area with the 13th-century grand mosque and clock tower. Watch your belongings.
Garden with flowering plants and walkways, open 06:00-20:00 per Wikivoyage.
Garden and cafe on the south side of the medina.
National forest with hiking and a view over the city.

stay: No sourced accommodation information for this town yet. Use the Booking.com, Airbnb or Google Maps buttons above.
food: No sourced food information for this town yet.
scams: No town-specific warnings sourced. See the Scams page in the Guide.
cities.transport: Not sourced yet. Check local transport options before you go.

cities.name: Tafraoute
cities.tagline: Anti-Atlas town known for hiking and rock landscapes.
cities.best: Not sourced. Check the weather before you go.

sights.n: Chapeau de Napoleon and Rochers Peints
sights.note: Hike out into the desert to these rock formations.
2-3 hour loop through a river bed southeast of town, past the village rock. Gazelles can sometimes be seen.
Tafraout Adventure on the main square gives maps, treks and bike rental.

stay: No sourced accommodation information for this town yet. Use the Booking.com, Airbnb or Google Maps buttons above.
food: No sourced food information for this town yet.
scams: No town-specific warnings sourced. See the Scams page in the Guide.
cities.transport: Not sourced yet. Check local transport options before you go.

cities.name: Skoura
cities.tagline: Oasis with a palm grove and rammed-earth kasbahs near Ouarzazate.
cities.best: Not sourced. Check the weather before you go.

scams.d: Someone offers to guide you for free then leads you to a shop for commission. Official guides carry a badge. Say a firm 'la, shukran' and keep walking.
Common in the Marrakech and Fes medinas. It is a lie to redirect you. Check on your map.
Petit taxis must use the meter. If the driver refuses, wait for another. Agree the full price before moving if there is no meter.
They may say your hotel is closed or that tickets are sold out. Buy tickets only at the official window. CTM and Supratours charge a small luggage fee; do not pay for a bag that fits in the cabin.
Do not let anyone start henna on your hand or put an animal on you without agreeing the price first. Ask before you take photos of performers.
Check the price of drinks before you order, especially on tourist squares.
Offers of hash are everywhere in tourist areas. Drug laws are strict for tourists and these offers are often a scam or police bait. Say no.
Use banks, official exchange offices or ATMs. Count the money. Keep exchange receipts if you want to change dirhams back. Max 2,000 MAD may leave the country (Wikivoyage).

tips: Currency is the dirham (MAD). Carry small notes and coins. Hotels and taxis often have no change.
You cannot buy dirhams outside Morocco. Max 2,000 MAD may leave the country (Wikivoyage).
Do not drink tap water. Bottled water is cheap.
Trains are the best way to travel between the big cities (ONCF). Buy on oncf-voyages.ma, not on re-seller sites with mark-ups (Wikivoyage).
Buy CTM or Supratours bus tickets at the official window.
Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) especially in the medina and in the countryside.
Public displays of affection and same-sex relations are legal risks in Morocco.
Friday lunch is traditional couscous day in many restaurants.
